thread:
maya patel: Heads up — customer-reported spike in 5xxs (primarily 503) hitting /v1/generate on hosted. Started ~1719823400, right after the feature flip that enabled prefetch routing and the auth-propagation flag.
jon kim: Seen it on our side too. Dashboard shows 3.8% 503 across frontend gateway in us-west-2 since 1719823420.
incident-bot: Alert: hosted/api -> 503 rate increased above threshold (3%) for 5m. Incident ID INC-2026-03017-01
sara nguyen: Which rollout went out? I think the feature flip for prefetch-routing:feature-prefetch-window = true landed in the last batch.
leo ortega: Correct. Also auth-propagation=fast-path was toggled in the same deploy to try to reduce latency for small payloads.
priya rao: Customer impact: several mid-market tenants reporting failures during inference calls, support ticket #SUP-4621. They're seeing timeouts followed by 503s.
maya patel: Quick repro from support: cURL to /v1/generate with body size ~4kb returns 200 then immediate 503 on retry. Logs show gateway upstream timed out while waiting for backend.
jon kim: Pasting relevant excerpt from gateway logs:
```
[1719823472] gw-502 pod-7f: upstream request to runtime-12 timed out after 6.0s, route=route-prefetch-2, req_id=abc123
[1719823472] gw-502 pod-7f: backend returned 503 when draining inflight after timeout
```
leo ortega: That timeout value aligns with the new prefetch window behavior — backend keeps warm connections but we may be exhausting concurrent slots due to earlier auth fast-path branching.
sara nguyen: Can someone check runtime p95 latency around that time? I see a small bump but not enough to explain 3.8% 503 unless we have queuing at the gateway.
priya rao: I queried telemetry: runtime p95 increased from 120ms -> 620ms for the small payload cohort at 1719823450-1719823550.
jon kim: Aha. If runtime p95 jumped to 600ms, and gateway timeout is 6000ms it shouldn't 503 that much — but if connections pile up behind slow auth propagation, shedder may be tripping.
maya patel: Support note: customers who hit the 503s were using short timeouts client-side — so they saw immediate failure and retried, amplifying load.
leo ortega: Immediate mitigation proposal: 1) Roll back auth-propagation=fast-path (flip false) on staging then prod canary. 2) Temporarily disable prefetch-routing for route-prefix /v1/generate to stop the new code path.
jon kim: I'll prepare rollback patch. Rolling auth-propagation back first — lower blast radius. Setting canary weight to 0 for that flag.
sara nguyen: Also open a throttling rule on the gateway for the affected route to protect runtime while we triage.
priya rao: Support: telling customers to throttle retries for 60s and we'll keep them posted. Adding contact for SUP-4621.
incident-bot: Action log: rollback auth-propagation scheduled by jon kim at 1719823660. Throttle rule request submitted by sara nguyen.
maya patel: After rollback (jon), let's monitor 503 rate and p95 for the next 10m. If it's still high, we pause the prefetch flag as well.
jon kim: Rolled back auth-propagation flag on canary at 1719823690, propagation confirmed.
leo ortega: Seeing 503 rate drop in canary region. Global still elevated — rolling a full rollback of auth-propagation now.
priya rao: Noting: support ticket updated with timeline and mitigation steps.
sara nguyen: Gateway throttle in place. Monitoring dashboards show downward trajectory for 503s.
maya patel: Closing loop: once 503s are back to baseline, we need a postmortem: root cause hypothesis — interaction between prefetch routing and auth fast-path causing head-of-line blocking and a spike in runtime p95 for small payloads, amplifying client retries.
jon kim: Agreed. Assigning follow-ups: runtime team to add better backpressure, infra to adjust shedder thresholds, product to review flag rollout checklist (include canary traffic isolation). I'll open INC-PR-503-171982 with owners.
support-bot: SUP-4621 updated: mitigation applied, customers notified. :white_check_mark:
maya patel: Thanks all. We'll keep monitoring for 30m then start a postmortem write-up.
